target_customer: Individual taxpayers in Colombia (originally pitched for Latin America) who must file income tax returns
problem: Few individuals in Latin America file taxes because accountants charge high fees and manual filing is error prone, and tax law changes often.
business_model: Consumer fee per tax filing, with expert-assisted filing, a business package and referrals of financial services

founders.name: Andrés Vélez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as former Head of Strategy at Rappi and a former private equity investor; LAVCA coverage says he worked alongside Rappi CEO Simon Borrero.

founders.name: Simón González
founders.background_notes: No background found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Tax calculation rules for one country plus integration with the DIAN tax authority data; mostly standard web engineering with domain rule work.

defensibility.rationale: Tax rules and DIAN integration are copyable, though seasonal scale and customer data give a modest edge. No lock-in beyond annual repeat use.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent software player was found acting in the segment in sources opened; the company is still active as of 2026 and reports covering 100 percent of individual tax cases in Colombia.

market_need_then: VentureBeat in March 2018 said only about 8 percent of individuals in Latin America file taxes, attributed to cost, with accountants charging roughly $100 per filing and a recent Colombian tax reform forcing rule changes.

branding.domain_note: Uses tributi.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Clara, an AI agent for tax questions (current site)

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as TurboTax for Latin America
branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions in Portafolio, El Tiempo, Semana and Inc (Inc 2019 list of startups that changed the world, per its site); no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press coverage and the TurboTax comparison give recognition in Colombia, with little evidence beyond that.

outcome_analysis: Tributi focused on Colombian individual tax filing after YC, raised an $800K seed in July 2018 and has stayed active. A 2024 Forbes Colombia piece reports more than 300,000 filings with most revenue in three months of tax season. The regional scope narrowed to Colombia, and later funding is not found in sources opened, so the outcome is a small but active business.
notes: Competitor search found no rival named in dated sources near the batch (VentureBeat and LAVCA coverage name none), so the list is empty. Aggregators disagree on seed: PitchBook $1M in 2018-06, Caplight $920K total, Latka claims no outside funding; only the $800K LAVCA figure is recorded as a round. The 300,000 filings figure is from the Forbes Colombia headline, not opened in full.
